first.rationale: With only one experiment slot, the highest-leverage move addresses two concurrent internal metrics (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) that prior consolidated memories (31, 86, 91) show respond durably to onboarding simplification and in-product activation nudges—both self-serve, low-risk, and previously shown to lift adoption without retention harm. The competitor's aggressive entry pricing creates pressure to respond with promotional_pricing, but memory_73 explicitly warns that targeted promo pricing boosts acquisition while materially hurting 30-day retention, undermining the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I verify memory_73 to confirm this tradeoff before ruling out pricing moves, and memory_86 to confirm the onboarding-completion evidence is robust before committing the week's only slot to it. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) and referral incentives (memory_57) are valid but don't address this quarter's most urgent, measurable degradations (activation/onboarding), so they're deprioritized rather than discarded. This is not a broad rollout because it's a fresh experiment cycle responding to a new quarter's decline, not a confirmed durable win yet at this scale/context; it's not a small_guarded_test because the underlying mechanism is already well-supported by two independent prior consolidations, warranting a standard experiment to confirm it still holds under current competitive conditions.

final.rationale: Verification confirms exp_86: shortened onboarding drove completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and retention +3% — a clean win with no downstream harm, directly addressing this quarter's onboarding completion decline (-4%) and contributing to activation (-6%) via faster time-to-value, consistent with memory_31 and memory_91. Verification of exp_73 confirms the earlier warning: targeted discounting produced signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% short-term, but 30-day retention -12%, with the acquired cohort failing to survive first renewal — explicitly not sustainable. Given the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, responding to the competitor's aggressive entry pricing with promotional pricing would trade durable revenue for a cohort that churns before renewal, which is the opposite of the objective. Onboarding simplification instead directly repairs the two internal metrics that degraded this quarter, has confirmed positive retention effects, and compounds with prior activation-messaging gains. This is scaled as a standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because although the mechanism is doubly confirmed historically, current-quarter conditions (competitive pricing pressure, declining baseline activation) differ enough from prior test conditions to warrant re-validation before full rollout; it is not a small_guarded_test because the strength and consistency of prior evidence justifies more than a minimal pilot. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives remain valid but lower urgency given they don't address the acute onboarding/activation declines this week.
